cve_validity.CVE-2026-3872: VALID — NVD status 'Modified After Enrichment' (Initial Analysis by NIST 2026-04-16); NOT rejected, NOT disputed. Red Hat CNA, CVSS 3.1 7.3 HIGH. Fix PR keycloak#47788, releases 26.2.15 / 26.4.11 / 26.5.7 / 26.6.0.

incomplete_fix_quote: CVE-2026-3872: Redirect URI validation bypass via ..;/ path traversal in OIDC auth endpoint. A flaw was found in Keycloak. This issue allows an attacker, who controls another path on the same web server, to bypass the allowed path in redirect URIs that use a wildcard. A successful attack may lead to the theft of an access token, resulting in information disclosure. It is the incomplete-fix residual of CVE-2024-1132, whose UNSAFE_PATH_PATTERN caught `../` but not the `..;/` matrix-parameter variant.
root_cause: org.keycloak.protocol.oidc.utils.RedirectUtils.UNSAFE_PATH_PATTERN. The CVE-2024-1132 fix (24.0.3) added this regex to reject `..` traversal in redirect_uri.getRawPath(), but its trailing-delimiter group only listed (/|%2f|%5c|\), omitting `;`. So `/allowed/..;/pwn` is NOT matched -> the `/allowed/*` wildcard still validates it -> redirect escapes the /allowed/ base to an attacker-controlled path. CVE-2026-3872 fix adds `|;` to that group.
sink_classification: reaching an unintended/attacker-controlled redirect target (open-redirect -> access-token exfil). NOT arbitrary file-read. Reproducible on Linux (no Windows/OS dependency; pure regex/URL-path logic). Differential is Keycloak redirect_uri ACCEPT vs REJECT, observed via a prompt=none 302 to the attacker sidecar.

patch_refs.v1_to_v2_3872_fix: keycloak <=26.5.6 -> 26.5.7, RedirectUtils.java: add `|;` to the trailing delimiter group (PR #47788)

mechanism_note: V0 (24.0.2) validated the DECODED+normalized redirect path against the wildcard (decodeRedirectUri + URI.normalize); `/allowed/x/..%2fpwn` normalizes to `/allowed/pwn` and passes. The CVE-2024-1132 fix (24.0.3) instead matches the RAW path and disables wildcards when UNSAFE_PATH_PATTERN matches, so the encoded `..%2f` is rejected. The residual `..;/` is not in the V1 delimiter set, so it slips past on V1 and is only closed by adding `|;` in 26.5.7.
